title: Ber (Zizyphus/Borehannu): modeled ₹361/qtl left, Dhanotu (Mandi) → Kangra (Baijnath)
summary: February 2021: reported ber (Zizyphus/Borehannu) prices at Dhanotu (Mandi) and Kangra (Baijnath) imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 82% of 17 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹361 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 6 same-variety market pairs screened for ber (Zizyphus/Borehannu) in February 2021; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Medium) at both markets; sale matched to the first Kangra (Baijnath) report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: February 2021
scenes.caption: Dhanotu (Mandi) (Himachal Pradesh) and Kangra (Baijnath) (Himachal Pradesh) both reported ber (Zizyphus/Borehannu) prices for the same variety and grade (Medium) on 17 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Dhanotu (Mandi) reported a median ₹2,600 per quintal. Kangra (Baijnath) reported a median ₹3,250 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹600/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹600 per quintal, and Kangra (Baijnath) was dearer on 94% of days.

scenes.headline: 150 km by road
scenes.caption: 150 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~3 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹32/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹272 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹107 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Kangra (Baijnath) report, the rule selects 14 of 17 modeled shipping days. 13 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹361 per quintal (₹190 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Ber (Zizyphus/Borehannu) route from Dhanotu (Mandi) to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 82% of matched days in February 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹36,100, or ₹19,000 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to ber (Zizyphus/Borehannu)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹32/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Ber (Zizyphus/Borehannu) route from Dhanotu (Mandi) to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 82% of matched days in February 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹36,100, or ₹19,000 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
